blocks.heading: What today is
blocks.body: About 80 minutes. Do the lab in the app. The check at the end uses words from today only.

blocks.heading: A page is a file
blocks.body:
Yesterday you opened the app. Today you open a **page**. A page is just a file. This course ships a tiny sample shop called flower-docs. You will write into it, not into a blank desktop file.

**File > Open** → `samples/flower-docs/topics/hello-concept.dita`.

The big middle area is where you type. Add one sentence. **Save**. Close. Open it again. If the sentence is still there, you did the job.

items.title: Word today
items.body: **Topic** :  one help page in its own file. Today you edited a topic. You do not need other kinds of pages yet.

items.title: If the file will not open
items.body: Use File > Open, not drag-onto-Slack. The file name should end in `.dita`. If Oxygen asks which type it is, pick a DITA topic.

blocks.title: Getting Started with Oxygen XML Editor
watchFor: How a page looks in the big middle area

blocks.heading: Do the work
blocks.body:
This lab can fail. Fail when: You typed in a notes app instead of Oxygen, or you did not save, or the sentence is gone after reopen.

Expected: The sample file opens, the extra sentence is there after save and reopen, and you wrote the path down.

blocks.intro: Walk the steps in order. Tick them in the lab after you actually do them.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.body: In Oxygen: File > Open. Open samples/flower-docs/topics/hello-concept.dita from this course.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.body: Click in the big writing area. Add this sentence under the first paragraph: The desk copy is a sample, not a live catalog.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: Save (Ctrl+S or Cmd+S). Confirm the file name in the tab still ends with .dita.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: Close the file. Open it again. Your sentence should still be there.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.body: Write the full path of the file in oxygen-bootcamp-work/day-02-path.txt.

blocks.summary: The sample file opens, the extra sentence is there after save and reopen, and you wrote the path down.

blocks.q: How do you open a page that already exists?
blocks.why: File > Open picks a file on disk. Help > About is only the version.

blocks.q: You typed a sentence and the tab still shows the file name. What should you do before you quit?
options: Save, then open the file again to check
blocks.why: If it is not saved, it is not in the file. Reopen is how you prove it.
